title: Effective-name discipline (corrected ?? snapshot) applied to the sweep and detail payload but NOT to the two reads feeding user-facing referee copy — the post-correction referee form and the new exhaustion notification name the REPLACED referee
evidence: sweep_due_reference_calls.sql:31 aliases the effective name — `COALESCE(NULLIF(rc.corrected_name, ''), rc.contact_name) AS contact_name` — so the post-correction invite EMAIL addresses the corrected referee (this PR's own §8.3 note: 'a landlord-corrected name must flow into the fresh invite').

get_form_context_by_form_token.sql:13 selects the RAW snapshot `rc.contact_name`; form_handler.copy_vars feeds it to form_copy.q_identity ('Are you ' <> referee_name <> '?') and landing_wrong_person ('Not ' <> referee_first_name <> ...) on the SSR form landing page (form_pages.gleam:135 renders the /reference/:token/wrong-person link on that page). After a correction, the referee's own form asks 'Are you <replaced name>?'.

That stale identity question now has a terminal consequence: apply_wrong_person (form_handler.gleam:1217) exhausts when `row.correction_cycles >= 1` — exactly the post-correction state — terminalizing the row to unreachable + stamping referee_contact_invalid (rc3-7's signal). An honest corrected referee answering 'No, this isn't me' to the stale name kills the row and fabricates the fraud signal.

find_reference_call_by_send_ref.sql:19 also selects the RAW snapshot; both exhaustion call sites pass it to the NEW notify_reference_correction_exhausted — webhooks.gleam:487 (`row.contact_name`) and form_handler.gleam:1309 (`row.contact_name`) — so 'Couldn't reach {name} ({applicant}'s referee)' names the replaced referee, not the corrected contact that actually failed.
impact: User-facing copy (form identity question + landlord notification) names the wrong person after any name correction, and the form's stale identity question can drive the honest corrected referee into the wrong-person route, which this PR made terminal (unreachable + fabricated referee_contact_invalid stamp).
recommendation: Apply the same effective-name COALESCE(NULLIF(corrected_name,''), contact_name) alias to get_form_context_by_form_token.sql and find_reference_call_by_send_ref.sql that sweep_due_reference_calls.sql uses, so the form greeting/identity question and the exhaustion notification address the referee the row is actually contacting.

title: Stale redelivered failure events (lost-ack retries) can exhaust a post-correction row and fabricate the referee_contact_invalid fraud signal
evidence: The webhook's only dedupe is live-status scoping (webhooks.gleam:248: 'the live-status scoping is the real dedup'); event_id is used only in Sentry tags (webhooks.gleam:351). Svix redelivers with the same message id when an ack is lost; Twilio retries StatusCallback on non-2xx with the same MessageSid:status.

find_reference_call_by_send_ref.sql matches `rc.attempts @> send_ref_json` (the pre-correction send's {outcome:'delivered', detail:<provider_id>} entry), scoped to status IN ('queued','contact_initiated').
correct_reference_call.sql never touches the attempts log, so the old send's delivered entry persists after the correction re-queues the row (cycles=1, status back in queued/contact_initiated).

A redelivered failure event for the PRE-correction send therefore re-enters apply_delivery_failure, finds the row, hits the new `row.correction_cycles >= 1` branch (webhooks.gleam:285), and exhaust_reference_call's guard (status IN ('queued','contact_initiated')) passes — the row is terminalized to unreachable and referee_contact_invalid is stamped, even though the corrected contact was never contacted (or its failure never observed). Pre-PR, the same stale event merely bounced the row back to awaiting_correction (recoverable; the documented W1 tradeoff).
impact: A lost-ack redelivery landing inside the correction window terminalizes a live check and stamps a fraud signal the AD-7 discipline says is 'never fabricated' — a false positive on a row whose fresh invite may be healthy.
recommendation: Gate the exhaustion branch on the failure belonging to the row's LATEST send (e.g. only exhaust when the matched send_ref equals the newest delivered entry in the attempts log / the current form_token's send), or restore an event-id dedupe so a processed failure can never be re-applied after a correction.

title: Substituted referee rows skip the rc3-7 creation-time fraud screening the trigger applies to every created row
evidence: The trigger's create path computes and stamps creation-time fraud signals on every new row — stamp_one_creation_fraud → sql.stamp_creation_fraud_signals (trigger.gleam:335) — covering cross-application contact reuse, duplicate-of-applicant, and the Twilio line-type lookup (AD-10: these signals run 'at capture'/creation).

substitute_reference_call.sql's INSERT creates a new live row (status default 'queued') with none of that: no stamp_creation_fraud_signals call anywhere in do_substitute, so the successor's fraud_signals column stays NULL and the new referee's contact is never screened for cross-application reuse or duplicate-of-applicant, and no line-type lookup runs.
impact: Fraud-lens blind spot on substituted referees: a contact reused across applications or a VOIP/burner number enters the pipeline with zero creation-time signals, diverging from the row-creation discipline every other creation path (trigger start) follows.
recommendation: Run the same creation-time signal computation (cross-app reuse read + line-type lookup + stamp_creation_fraud_signals) on the substituted row's new trio, reusing the trigger's stamp_one_creation_fraud machinery.
